normativeSourceAccess.source: ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English, Issue 9, dated 2025-01-15, supplied to the project for review.
verifiedScope: All 53 writing-rule identifiers and section titles in Part 1.
The rule summaries and explanations needed to map the LUDWISE profile.
The distinction between writing rules and the general recommendations in section 9.
normativeSourceAccess.dictionaryUse: Part 2 was reviewed as the normative controlled dictionary. The repository does not copy or vendor the dictionary, and the local checker does not claim full lexical validation.
normativeSourceAccess.consequence: Phase 1 has a complete verified map of all 53 writing rules. Phase 2 must apply them to existing prose and make semantic review a blocking workflow requirement.

enforcementTypes.deterministic: A machine can decide the configured check from text and structure without semantic judgment.
enforcementTypes.heuristic: A machine can identify a probable issue, but a person must confirm it.
enforcementTypes.semantic: Correctness depends on meaning, grammar, domain terminology, or reader intent.
enforcementTypes.process: A required review or workflow step carries the rule.
enforcementTypes.not-applicable: The rule does not apply to the governed LUDWISE content.

standardRuleMap.title: Use approved dictionary words, technical nouns, or technical verbs.
standardRuleMap.limitation: The local checker has no complete controlled-dictionary source.

standardRuleMap.title: Use an approved word only as its approved part of speech.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Dictionary and grammatical review are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use an approved word only with its approved meaning.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Dictionary and semantic review are required. LW-STE-CAUSAL-SINCE reports one probable error in this rule, a since that reads as a reason, and it does not decide the rule.

standardRuleMap.title: Use only approved verb and adjective forms.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Dictionary and grammatical review are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use technical nouns only from permitted technical-noun categories.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Domain terminology review is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use a non-approved word only when it is a technical noun or part of one.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Dictionary and domain review are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Do not use a technical noun as a verb.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Part-of-speech and domain review are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use technical nouns approved for the applicable domain.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Domain terminology review is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Prefer short and clear technical nouns.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Clarity requires human review.

standardRuleMap.title: Do not use regional, slang, or jargon words as technical nouns.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Configured prohibited expressions catch known cases only.

standardRuleMap.title: Use one technical noun consistently for the same item.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Recorded synonyms are checked; referential identity still needs review.

standardRuleMap.title: Use technical verbs only from permitted technical-verb categories.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Domain terminology review is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Do not use a technical verb as a noun.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Part-of-speech and domain review are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use American English spelling unless an official directive requires another spelling.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Only configured spelling variants are checked.

standardRuleMap.title: Keep a multi-word noun to three words or fewer.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Reliable noun-phrase recognition requires grammar and domain context.

standardRuleMap.title: Handle a longer technical noun with the approved clarification method.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Domain terminology and prior-use context are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use only dictionary-listed verb forms.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Dictionary validation is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use only permitted verb forms and tenses.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Grammatical analysis is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use past participles as adjectives only in the permitted form.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Grammatical analysis is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Do not create prohibited complex verb constructions with auxiliaries.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Grammatical analysis is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use an -ing verb form only in permitted technical-noun roles.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Grammar and domain terminology are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use active voice; descriptive passive voice is allowed only when the agent is unknown.
standardRuleMap.limitation: The passive exception depends on meaning.

standardRuleMap.title: Describe an action with an approved verb.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Dictionary and semantic review are required.

standardRuleMap.title: Write short, clear, accurate sentences with one topic.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Length is measurable; clarity, accuracy, and topic count are semantic.

standardRuleMap.title: Do not omit necessary words or use contractions to shorten a sentence.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Contractions are checked; omitted necessary words require review.

standardRuleMap.title: Use a vertical list when complex text is clearer as a list.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Need for a list depends on meaning and structure.

standardRuleMap.title: Connect related sentences with suitable connecting words or phrases.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Logical relation is semantic.

standardRuleMap.title: Use an article or demonstrative adjective before a noun when applicable.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Applicability depends on grammar and context.

standardRuleMap.title: Limit each procedural sentence to 20 words.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Core word-count rules are implemented; some special elements require review.

standardRuleMap.title: Give one instruction per sentence unless actions occur at the same time.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Simultaneous-action meaning requires review.

standardRuleMap.title: Write procedure instructions in the imperative form.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Imperative-form analysis requires grammar and context.

standardRuleMap.title: Put a necessary condition before the command and separate it with a comma.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Condition scope requires semantic review.

standardRuleMap.title: Use notes for information only, not for instructions, requirements, or limits.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Note meaning requires semantic review.

standardRuleMap.title: Give descriptive information gradually.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Information progression is document-level semantics.

standardRuleMap.title: Use key words and key phrases to give descriptive text a logical structure.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Logical structure requires document-level review.

standardRuleMap.title: Limit each descriptive sentence to 25 words.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Core word-count rules are implemented; some special elements require review.

standardRuleMap.title: Use paragraphs to group related descriptive information.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Relatedness is semantic.

standardRuleMap.title: Keep one topic in each paragraph.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Topic count is semantic.

standardRuleMap.title: Limit each descriptive paragraph to six sentences.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Extracted sentence boundaries are checked; unusual embedded structures need review.

standardRuleMap.title: Identify the level of risk with the applicable safety word or symbol.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Risk classification requires domain judgment.

standardRuleMap.title: Start a safety instruction with a clear command or condition.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Safety meaning requires domain review.

standardRuleMap.title: Explain the risk or possible result in the safety instruction.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Risk/result accuracy requires domain review.

standardRuleMap.title: Use standard English punctuation but do not use a semicolon.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Semicolons outside exempt machine syntax are deterministic.

standardRuleMap.title: Use hyphens only to connect words that are directly related.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Semantic relation is required.

standardRuleMap.title: Use parentheses only for the purposes permitted by the standard.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Purpose of parentheses is semantic.

standardRuleMap.title: For word count in a vertical list, treat a colon as the end of a sentence.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Normal Markdown list structure is recognized; not every vertical-list form is inferable.

standardRuleMap.title: Count parenthetical text as one word in its containing sentence and count its sentence separately.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Balanced parenthetical prose is handled; malformed or unusual structures need review.

standardRuleMap.title: Count each specified special element as one word for sentence length.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Known numbers, units, names, identifiers, and quoted text are handled; not every proper noun, title, label, or unit is inferable.

standardRuleMap.title: Count a hyphenated word as one word.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Hyphenated tokens count as one word.

standardRuleMap.title: Change the sentence construction when word-for-word replacement is insufficient.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Safe reconstruction must preserve meaning.

standardRuleMap.title: Use each approved word correctly.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Approved meaning and part of speech require dictionary review.

standardRuleMap.title: Do not combine words to create a phrasal verb.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Recorded phrasal verbs are checked; complete detection requires language analysis.

standardRuleMap.title: Use terminology and wording consistently.
standardRuleMap.limitation: Full consistency is document-level semantics.

rules.title: Blocking enforcement requires an explicit procedural or descriptive prose kind.
rules.limitations: Audit mode can estimate list shape; enforcement never trusts that estimate.

rules.title: A procedural sentence has 20 words or fewer.
rules.limitations: Some special word-count elements require review.

rules.title: A descriptive sentence has 25 words or fewer.
rules.limitations: Some special word-count elements require review.

rules.title: A descriptive paragraph has six sentences or fewer.
Do not use a contraction to shorten controlled prose.
rules.limitations: Omitted necessary words still require review.

rules.title: Use the recorded preferred technical noun consistently for one concept.
rules.limitations: Only recorded synonym conflicts are deterministic.

rules.title: Do not use a recorded phrasal verb.
rules.limitations: Only recorded phrasal verbs are deterministic.

rules.title: Use the recorded American English spelling.
Do not use a semicolon in controlled prose.
Do not use an expression that the LUDWISE terminology policy prohibits.
rules.limitations: This is a closed LUDWISE list.

rules.title: Do not use an abbreviation prohibited by the LUDWISE policy.
Expand an abbreviation on first use when the LUDWISE policy requires it.
rules.limitations: This is a LUDWISE extension scoped to one file.

rules.title: Review a since that reads as a reason rather than as time.
rules.limitations: Issue 9 approves since as a conjunction of time and requires because for a reason. Nothing in the text marks the meaning, so this rule reads clause shape and excludes a following time expression. It cannot see a reason in another position, and it does not check the part of speech. Rule 1.3 stays a semantic review obligation, and this rule is an aid to that review rather than proof of it.

rules.title: Do not use a configured slash form to join alternatives.
Review an abbreviation that the LUDWISE policy does not record.
rules.limitations: Capitalized text has too many non-abbreviation meanings for a safe blocker.

rules.title: A code comment must state information that clearer code cannot state.
rules.limitations: Comment necessity is a review judgment.

rules.title: User-facing text follows the STE-derived pipeline without changing meaning.
rules.limitations: Visitor strings and semantic equivalence are not machine-checked.

rules.title: A governed file must be readable and parseable.
The language policy must be complete and well formed.
The terminology policy must be internally consistent.
The standard map and checker-control registry must agree with declared coverage.
Declared exemptions and implemented exemptions must match.
Every prose-bearing file must match an explicit classification.
A language exception must record all required fields and known rules.
An expired language exception must not remain active.
A language exception that matches no tracked file must be removed.

coverage.note: The normative map is complete. Machine enforcement remains intentionally partial where safe deterministic checking is not possible.
